1. Chunking logic

Docling’s visual nesting is unreliable for Hebrew legal PDFs (e.g. §3 and §2.3 both as list level 2). We rebuild hierarchy from section numbers in item text, then cut vectors for embedding.

Pipeline

flowchart LR A[PDF] --> B[Docling iterate_items] B --> C[Blocks + bbox] C --> D[Extract § refs from text] D --> E[Rebuild tree by number] E --> F[Group units] F --> G[Header attach] G --> H[Pack / split] H --> I[Vectors ~500 tok]
1. ParseDocling iterate_items() → blocks with page + bbox. Prefer structure over markdown export (RTL/OCR noise).
2. NumberExtract § refs (3.1.1) with heuristics; ignore Docling level. Reject mid-text quantities, dates, plan codes.
3. GroupConsecutive blocks with the same unit key: subclause → clause → section → orphan.
4. PackClause/subclause kept whole if ≤ max; section/orphan glued toward ~500 tok (max 700).
5. HeadersNever end a vector on a title; peel trailing headers onto the next body.

Decision: which unit becomes a vector?

flowchart TD S[Block run] --> D{Depth of § ref?} D -->|≥3| SC[subclause — emit if ≤ max] D -->|2| CL[clause — emit if ≤ max] D -->|1| SP[section_pack toward target] D -->|none| OP[orphan_pack toward target] SC --> OV{tokens > max?} CL --> OV OV -->|yes| SPL[split on block / char boundaries] OV -->|no| DONE[one vector] SP --> DONE OP --> DONE SPL --> DONE

Unit priority

  1. Sub-clause (§N.M.K+) — one vector if ≤ max tokens
  2. Clause (§N.M) — same; fold in consecutive descendants (§N.M.*) while the combined size stays ≤ max (keeps stems like §4.8 with §4.8.1/§4.8.2)
  3. Small siblings — consecutive tiny units packed toward ~500: clauses/subclauses that share a parent (e.g. §2.1+§2.2), and top-level sections (e.g. §5+§6)
  4. Section pack — remaining depth-1 / inherited §N body, glued until ~500 tokens
  5. Orphan pack — no section number; pack by page/order to ~500
  6. Split — only if a single unit exceeds max (700)

Packing rules (section / orphan)

  • Accumulate blocks until adding the next would exceed target and the buffer is already ≥ 40% of target.
  • A header always starts a new pack (stays with the following body).
  • Before flushing, peel any trailing header into the next pack.
  • A single block > max is hard-split by character length approx. to max tokens.

Header rule

  • A SectionHeaderItem (or short numbered title ≤ 90 chars) starts a pack — it is not appended onto the previous full pack.
  • If a pack would end on a header, the header is peeled onto the next vector.
  • A lone §N title merges into the following §N.M clause when present.

Section-number extraction (parse)

  • Prefer a dotted self-ref at the start/end of the line over cross-refs mid-sentence.
  • Reject patterns that look like quantities (3.5 טון), dates, or plan codes.
  • Tree parent/child comes from the numeric path (2.3.1 under 2.3), not Docling’s visual level.

Why not page-sized vectors?

Pages are ~1.5–2.5k tokens (p50/p95). That buries fine clauses (e.g. treatment limits). Retrieve top‑k vectors (~400–800 tok each) so generation still sees enough context. Clause p50 (~228) is below target; section p50 (~147) is tiny but mean/p95 explode — packing fills the gap.
